headline: Premier League finds Man City guilty of serious financial breaches
summary: The club is accused of artificially inflating revenues by over £900 million to bypass spending limits between 2009 and 2018.
details: Manchester City have been found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009 and 2018.
An independent commission found the club used sham contracts with commercial partners to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs, concealing the true state of their finances.
The schemes were found to have inflated revenues and reduced costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) to appear to comply with financial sustainability rules.
The commission also found the club guilty of the majority of charges regarding their failure to co-operate with the league's investigation over four years.
While no sanction has yet been imposed, potential penalties include points deductions, heavy fines, or even expulsion from the Premier League.
Manchester City expressed surprise at the decision and has vowed to appeal, claiming the opinion contains material errors of law, principle, and fact.
Since 2008, City has become a dominant force in English football, winning eight Premier League titles and the 2023 Champions League.
caption:
Man City found guilty of inflating revenues by over £900 million. Their place in the Premier League is now at risk.

Manchester City have been found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009 and 2018.

The schemes were found to have inflated revenues and reduced costs by more than £900 million ($1.2 billion) to appear to comply with financial sustainability rules.

The commission also found the club guilty of the majority of charges regarding their failure to co-operate with the league's investigation over four years.

While no sanction has yet been imposed, potential penalties include points deductions, heavy fines, or even expulsion from the Premier League.

Manchester City expressed surprise at the decision and has vowed to appeal, claiming the opinion contains material errors of law, principle, and fact.

Since 2008, City has become a dominant force in English football, winning eight Premier League titles and the 2023 Champions League.

headline_marked: 38 eminent citizens warn of [[rising attacks and land grabbing]]
headline: 38 eminent citizens warn of rising attacks and land grabbing
summary: A group of prominent figures demands impartial investigations into a surge of extortion and forced evictions carried out through political and muscle power.
details: A group of 38 eminent citizens has raised alarm over a surge in attacks, land and house grabbing, and extortion across Bangladesh, warning of a serious deterioration in law and order.
In a joint statement issued on Tuesday, the signatories demanded high-level, impartial investigations to identify those involved and their patrons, both at home and abroad.
The citizens cited several recent incidents, including the attack and looting at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1 and the looting of content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio in the ECB area.
Reports of forced evictions of landless people from chars in Patuakhali, Noakhali Sadar, and Bhola were also highlighted, with allegations that crops were looted at night through political influence.
The statement further noted an alarming rise in mugging in Dhaka and other cities, alongside child rape and violence against women.
The signatories alleged that influential quarters linked to political parties, armed followers of the ousted government, and sections of law enforcement agencies may be involved.
They expressed concern that in some areas, police were unable to act in time due to the alleged involvement of ruling-party leaders and activists.
The group called for the government as a whole, not just the home ministry, to be held accountable for the current security situation.
caption:
38 prominent citizens warn of a surge in land grabbing and extortion across Bangladesh. Is law and order deteriorating?

A group of 38 eminent citizens has raised alarm over a surge in attacks, land and house grabbing, and extortion across Bangladesh, warning of a serious deterioration in law and order.

In a joint statement issued on Tuesday, the signatories demanded high-level, impartial investigations to identify those involved and their patrons, both at home and abroad.

The citizens cited several recent incidents, including the attack and looting at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1 and the looting of content creator Salman Muqtadir’s studio in the ECB area.

Reports of forced evictions of landless people from chars in Patuakhali, Noakhali Sadar, and Bhola were also highlighted, with allegations that crops were looted at night through political influence.

The statement further noted an alarming rise in mugging in Dhaka and other cities, alongside child rape and violence against women.

The signatories alleged that influential quarters linked to political parties, armed followers of the ousted government, and sections of law enforcement agencies may be involved.

They expressed concern that in some areas, police were unable to act in time due to the alleged involvement of ruling-party leaders and activists.

The group called for the government as a whole, not just the home ministry, to be held accountable for the current security situation.
